title: Tiny error. Can you trust it at x = 3?
hook: A fit that is never off by more than 0.125. Is it right everywhere?

knows: that a model is fitted to data points
that held-out data checks for overfitting
doesNotKnow: that a fit can be good inside its data and badly wrong outside it

misconception: A model with a tiny error is right everywhere.
objective: The learner can explain that a model's error is only measured where its training data lived, so predictions for cases unlike the training data (here, outside 0 to 1) can be far off without any warning.

claims.text: The least-squares line through y = x² at x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 has slope 1 and intercept −0.125, and is off by at most 0.125 anywhere between 0 and 1.
claims.source: Mean x 0.5, mean y 0.375, Sxy = Sxx = 0.625. Error x² − x + 0.125 is +0.125 at 0 and 1 and −0.125 at 0.5. Reproduced by fit() and maxInsideError() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: At x = 3 the line predicts 2.875 while the truth is 9, a gap of 6.125 (at x = 2: 1.875 vs 4).
claims.source: line(3) = 3 − 0.125; truth(3) = 9. Node output of line() and truth() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: The truth y = x² is invented for the toy.
claims.source: Brief 28 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; labelled on the stage and in the reveal.

claims.text: A model is only tested where its data lived; predictions for inputs unlike the training data (dataset shift, extrapolation) can fail without the training error warning.
claims.source: About real systems: Quiñonero-Candela, Sugiyama, Schwaighofer & Lawrence (eds.) 2009, Dataset Shift in Machine Learning (MIT Press), ch. 1.

recall.question: A house-price model was trained on homes of 50-150 m² and has a small test error. Someone asks it to price a 600 m² mansion. What should you expect?
options: The estimate could be far off: no training home looked like this
About as accurate as its test error says
Exactly right, since bigger homes simply cost more
recall.why: Test error measures accuracy where the training data lived. Outside that range the model is extrapolating and its small error says nothing about it.
